package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after its domain was acquired by a new owner (Funnull). The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically delivered to all downstream consumers without their knowledge or consent.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the script is loaded by the browser)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Detects if the visitor is using a mobile device and, if so, redirects them to a scam website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user-agent sniffing and forcibly redirects users to an external, likely malicious, domain. This is not expected behavior for a polyfill library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill library should only provide compatibility shims for JavaScript features, not perform user-agent checks or redirects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User-agent checks and redirects may be used for legitimate mobile site redirection, but never in a third-party polyfill library loaded from a CDN.
key_indicators: Behavior embedded in a widely used third-party library

attack_chain.action: Website or npm package includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io (e.g., <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser loads and executes the JavaScript from the CDN

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is delivered from the compromised CDN endpoint
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the website visitor

attack_chain.action: Malicious code checks if the visitor is on a mobile device and redirects them to a scam site
attack_chain.leads_to: User is sent to a phishing or scam site, potentially leading to further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript performing user-agent sniffing and redirecting users
Unexpected window.location or document.location assignments in polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts containing code unrelated to feature detection or shimming
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in script tags or npm package source code
Polyfill JavaScript files containing redirect logic
network_indicators: Subsequent redirects to known scam or phishing domains from pages loading polyfill.io scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for inclusion of cdn.polyfill.io in web pages or npm package dependencies. Analyze loaded JavaScript for unexpected behaviors such as user-agent checks and redirects. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to block or report unexpected script sources. Employ Subresource Integrity (SRI) to ensure third-party scripts have not been tampered with. Flag any polyfill scripts that perform DOM manipulations or network requests unrelated to polyfill functionality.
